pronunciationGuide: Every word and every example sentence now has an orange phonetic guide in [brackets] underneath it, written using English spelling patterns so you can sound it out without learning IPA symbols. This is an approximation, not a precise phonetic transcription — Swedish has pitch-accent and vowel-length distinctions that English spelling can't fully capture. Use it to get close, then refine your ear with native audio (Forvo, YouTube, or a Swedish course with sound). Key: ah = father · eh = bed · ee = see · oo = boot · oh = for · ai = air · ur = fur (this covers ö) · ch = the 'k' sound in kött/kyckling (like German 'ch') · sh = the sj/skj/stj sound · y = both consonant j and the soft g (as in gilla). Stressed syllables are generally the first syllable of a word unless shown otherwise.
